findings.reason: naming whether the new comparator extends `_longest_contiguous_word_span`'s module or is genuinely a new one is what keeps the package's one-tokeniser rule from becoming a two-comparator rule, and it fixes the node's write scope.
findings.text: §22 introduces its own edit-share comparison (a word-level sequence matcher, "private to the review module") while the package already owns a word-level comparison over the same `_normalised_words` tokeniser, `_longest_contiguous_word_span` at dispatch.py:479 (called only by `_done_when_plan_overlap_warning`, dispatch.py:490), so two comparators over one tokeniser come to live in two modules (reckon/crew/plan_review.py and reckon/crew/dispatch.py); the section names where the tokeniser lives but not where the comparison lives, so the node's write scope and the package rule it applies are unstated. Census of word-comparison sites over `_normalised_words`: exactly one today (dispatch.py:479-496); §22 makes it two.

findings.reason: a node told to follow "the path §7 built" may add a fourth single-key carve-out beside the existing set-aside and validator rather than widen the one pattern, and the differing value shapes (integer vs closed-interval float) are exactly where a copied single-key check accepts the wrong type.
findings.text: §22 declares `review.plan_change_threshold`, 0.30, in `reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml` and says it is "the path §7 built for `review.plan_settle_seconds`", but names only the accessor consolidation; the path it points at is three separate single-key sites — the schema set-aside that drops the key before the review schema's forbid-extra check (reckon/flight.py:322), the `validate_layer` check that a declared key is a non-negative integer (reckon/flight.py:863-867), and the accessor (reckon/flight.py:684) — and the threshold is a float in [0,1] where settle is a non-negative integer, so each of the three must be widened, not merely pointed at. The section does not enumerate the two sites it does not name.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16 concentrates span-finding, body extent and boundary resolution behind one `section_prose` reader plus the existing `_section_digests`, and deletes `_AuthoredProseParser`; the change is a net reduction (public_definitions 1481 → 1481 across the second node), which is the direction the rubric asks for.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §22's prose measure needs the reviewed snapshot's per-unit text, which §21's coverage predicate does not hand out, so the snapshot is located and read a second time outside §21's "one owner"; and §22 adds a second word-level comparator over the one tokeniser `dispatch._normalised_words` without naming the owner of the existing comparator.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; all four open sections name, in their own text, what they retire or merge or why the family stays level (§16: stripper public→private for `section_prose`; §21: no public definition added or retired; §22: `plan_review_settings` added, `plan_review_settle_seconds` retired; §23: `store_delivered_reviews` added, `store_delivered_report` private, private loop retired).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the open sections (§16 second node, §21, §22, §23) each cite the existing mechanism they extend and I opened every one: `_plan_html._TAG_RE` and `count_open_decisions` (reckon/_plan_html.py:1876-1909), `structured_section_spans` (reckon/_plan_html.py:415, callers reckon/_store.py:827,1466), `_prose_slices` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:148), `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates`, `roadmap.implementable_sections`, `list_plan_reviews`, `review_report_directory` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:791), and `dispatch._normalised_words` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:289) all exist as described.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two accessors that could be thin layers are replacements rather than additions: §22 retires `plan_review_settle_seconds` (reckon/flight.py:684) for `plan_review_settings`, and §23 retires the public store loop's second copy by hoisting it, each naming what it retires in the section text.
